summary: Charles Ramble works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Durham University and Oxford (D.Phil. 1981) under Michael Aris. He served as professor at Oxford (~2000–2010) and Directeur d'études at École Pratique des Hautes Études (2009).

Charles Rieu specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Geneva and Bonn (doctorate 1840–1843) under Lassen, Humbert, Freytag, and Gildemeister. He served at the British Museum (1847) and Cambridge as Adams Professor of Arabic.

Lanman was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale and in Berlin, Tübingen, and Leipzig under Whitney, Weber, and Roth. He taught at Johns Hopkins (1876–1880) and served as professor at Harvard University from 1880 to 1926.

Charles S. Prebish is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Case Western Reserve University and under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Pennsylvania State University (~1981–2007).

Charles Taliaferro is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, Harvard Divinity School, the University of Rhode Island, and Brown University. He served as a professor at St. Olaf College from around 1985 to 2022.

Charles Taylor is a philosopher who studied at McGill University and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as Professor of Political Science at McGill University (~1961–1998) and held posts at the Université de Montréal (~1967–1971) and Northwestern University (~2002–2007).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1959) and the University of Illinois System (~1965–1969), and he held a post at Ohio University (~1968–1972).

Charles Wilkins worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Kalinatha (~1778–1785). He served as librarian for the East India Company and the India Office Library, and he founded the Asiatic Society in 1784.
Charles Willemen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under William Reynolds Beal Acker. He held a professorship at Ghent University, attested from 1999 to 2001.

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Indology. After earning a law doctorate at Liège, he served as professor at KU Leuven / Université catholique de Louvain from ~1867 to 1899.

Chatral Sangye Dorje was a Buddhist and Tibetology master. He studied under Sera Khandro Dewé Dorje, Dorje Dradul, Ngawang Palzang, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, among others, and eventually succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned degrees from Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities. From ~1973 to 2000, she served in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Thammasat University.
Chen Ming is a scholar in Indology, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He has held a post as professor at Peking University, attested in 2001 and 2013.

Chen-kuo Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his studies at Temple University in 1991. He served as professor and distinguished professor at National Chengchi University and held the European Chair of Chinese Studies at Leiden University.
Cheryl A. Crowley is a scholar in the field of Japanology. She studied under Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip Boas Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.

Chhimed Rigdzin was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under and taught Choying Khyabdel. He conducted research at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and served as Professor of Tibetan at Visva-Bharati University (~1957–1987).
Chhimed Rigdzin Rinpoche was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held a post at Visva-Bharati University.

Chi Chen Ho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under traditional teacher Hsuan Hua, earned a Ph.D. under Robert Buswell at UCLA in 2010, and served as a teaching assistant there.
Chi-chen Wang was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from ~1922 to 1924. He held a post at Columbia University from ~1929 to 1965.

Chi-chiang Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986, studying under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao and under Robert M. Gimello.
